cat > app/Http/Controllers/LocaleController.ts <<'EOF'
import { Controller } from '@guren/core'

const ONE_YEAR_SECONDS = 60 * 60 * 24 * 365

export default class LocaleController extends Controller {
  async store(): Promise<Response> {
    const { body } = this.validated('locale.store')
    const cookie = `locale=${body.locale}; Path=/; Max-Age=${ONE_YEAR_SECONDS}; SameSite=Lax`
    return this.redirect(this.backUrl(), { headers: { 'Set-Cookie': cookie } })
  }

  // Only same-origin Referers are followed, so the switcher is not an open redirect.
  private backUrl(): string {
    const referer = this.request.header('Referer')
    if (!referer) return '/'
    try {
      const target = new URL(referer, this.request.url)
      return target.origin === new URL(this.request.url).origin
        ? `${target.pathname}${target.search}`
        : '/'
    } catch {
      return '/'
    }
  }
}
EOF

result:
Japanese is added alongside English, with a language switcher in the header on every page. `bun run typecheck`, `bun test` (6 pass, including the new locale tests) and `guren check --i18n` all pass. I did not run the app or check the pages in a browser.

- **`POST /locale`:** the route is open to guests and signed-in users.
  - It sets a one-year `locale` cookie and redirects to the `Referer` path, or `/` when there is none.
  - A cross-origin `Referer` also falls back to `/`.
  - `fr` or a missing field returns 422, the same way an invalid post title does, and the cookie is left alone.
- **Language detection:** `src/app.ts` now lists `['en', 'ja']`. The framework already checks `?locale=`, then the cookie, then `Accept-Language`, so a pick beats the browser and a Japanese browser gets `ja`. `_i18n.locale` reflects this.
- **Catalogs:** there are `lang/en` and `lang/ja` files for `messages` (the existing `welcome` line), `nav`, `auth` and `posts`. Each file is its own namespace, so the keys read exactly `nav.home`, `posts.new`, `auth.logout` and so on. All nine Japanese values from your table are in, and both catalogs have the same 28 keys.
- **Frontend:**
  - The header (`Layout.tsx`) reads its labels from the catalog and now has a Home link and an English/日本語 dropdown.
  - The posts list, post page, and new and edit forms read from the catalog too. That includes search-error text and the delete confirmation. No page spells out 「記事」 itself.
- **Tests:** `tests/LocaleController.test.ts` covers the cookie and redirect, the no-`Referer` case, `fr` and missing-field rejection, and Accept-Language versus the cookie.

The dashboard, login, register and profile pages still have hard-coded English, since you only asked for the header and posts pages. Also, the English catalog keeps the existing labels ("Write", "Sign in", "Log out"), so those stay as they are today.

The new code is in `app/Http/Controllers/LocaleController.ts`, `app/Http/Validators/LocaleValidator.ts`, `routes/web.ts` and `lang/`. I regenerated the `.guren` files with codegen.
